title: Family of FSU mass shooting victim files lawsuit alleging ChatGPT helped shooter
key_facts: Attorneys for the family of Tiru Chabba, killed in the Florida State University shooting, filed a federal lawsuit against OpenAI and ChatGPT in the US District Court for the Northern District of Florida; suspect Phoenix Ikner is also named.
The complaint alleges OpenAI could have done more to prevent the shooting.
According to ChatGPT logs released by Florida law enforcement, Ikner allegedly asked ChatGPT about gun operations, media coverage and the busiest time on campus.
Family attorney Bakari Sellers says the messages go back about 18 months and include 16,000 'disturbing chats'.

OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said ChatGPT is not responsible, gave factual answers from public sources, did not encourage harm, and that OpenAI identified an account believed linked to the suspect and shared it with law enforcement.
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier said on 21 April that state prosecutors opened a criminal investigation into OpenAI and ChatGPT.

The shooting on 17 April 2025 injured six and killed two, Chabba and Robert Morales; Ikner pleaded not guilty to two counts of first-degree murder and seven of attempted murder, with trial set for October 2026.
quote_evidence: The complaint, which was filed on Sunday in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida, also names the shooting suspect, Phoenix Ikner, as a defendant.
ChatGPT is not responsible for this terrible crime.
alleging that the company could have done more to prevent the shooting
why_it_matters_hint: A victim's family is testing whether a chatbot maker can be held responsible for what a user did, but the claims are unproven.
event_date: Lawsuit filed Sunday 10 May 2026 (article says 'Sunday'; May date from other outlets' listings); shooting 17 Apr 2025.
